Date: 2022-02-25
REMARKS
This Amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated October 27, 2021. Applicant has amended claims 1, 13, and 23 and added claims 27-31. Claims 1-31 are pending upon entry of this communication.
Interview Summary
As a preliminary matter, Applicant thanks the Examiner for the telephonic interview conducted on November 8, 2021. Participating in the interview were Examiners Shreya Parag Anj aria and Mallika D. Fairchild, and Applicant's representatives, Jason D. Kelly (Reg. No. 54,213) and Zachary Y. Zhou (Reg. No. 79,187). During the interview, the parties discussed the rejection of claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 101. No agreements were reached during the interview. No exhibits were submitted, and no demonstrations were performed.
Claim Reiection Under 35 U.S.C. 101
The Office Action rejected claims 1-26 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 based on an assertion that these claims are directed to non-statutory subject matter. Without conceding the merits of the rejections, and in the interest of advancing prosecution to an indication of allowance, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 13, and 23. For instance, amended independent claim 1 recites "processing circuitry configure to... determine a PVC detection quantification for the patient based on the determinations that the plurality of ventricular depolarizations are PVCs; and communication circuitry configured to transmit data comprising the PVC detection quantification determined by the processing circuitry to a user computing device," functions that clearly cannot be practically performed in the mind. Independent claims 13 and 23 have been amended in a similar fashion. Therefore, Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections, particularly to the extent the rejections may be considered applicable to the claims as amended. The following remarks are not to be used for claim construction or any other similar purpose, but are presented solely in connection with traversing the 35 U.S.C. § 101 rejection.
Notwithstanding the above, Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Office that the original independent claims 1, 13, and 23 are directed to patent-ineligible subject matter. In the Office Action, the Office asserted that "identifying PVC can include a healthcare professional visually identifying a maximum and minimum slope point . .. nothing in the elements of the claims precludes the step from practically being performed in the mind." However, contrary to the Office's assertions, the elements of independent claims 1, 13, and 23 cannot conceivably be performed in the mind.
For example, the original independent claim 1 recites processing circuitry configured to identify "a maximum slope point, a minimum slope point, and an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point... [and] determine that the current ventricular depolarization is a premature ventricular contraction (PVC) depolarization based on the intervals from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point satisfying the one or more slope criteria." A cardiac electrogram signal includes rapid and complex slope changes. The Office has not provided any evidence or rationale supporting the assertion that a healthcare professional could visually identify maximum and minimum slope points in the signal. Nor has the Office demonstrated that the calculations required to determine the slope of the cardiac electrogram or satisfaction of the slope criteria can be entirely performed in the human mind or even with pencil and paper. Indeed, regarding identifying the maximum slope point and minimum slope point, cardiac electrograms are not simple mathematical functions that are amenable to differentiation by the human mind. Rather, cardiac electrograms are Fourier series that are far more complex than the quadratic expressions typically in a Calculus textbook.
Hence, it is impractical for a human to perform the numerous and frequently difficult calculations necessary to identify a maximum slope point, a minimum slope point, and an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point as well as determine satisfaction of slope criteria without utilization of a machine. As such, the processing circuitry recited in the original claims is essential to the operation of the original claims such that the elements of the original claims cannot be practically performed in the mind.
For at least these reasons, claims 1-26 recite patentable subject matter under 35 U.S.C. § 101. Applicant therefore respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.
1 Office Action dated October 27, 2021, page 4.
New Claims
Applicant has added claims 27-31 to the pending application. The applied references fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's new claims, and would have provided no apparent reason for modification to arrive at the claimed features. No new matter has been added by the new claims.
CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.
Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
Please charge any additional fees or credit any overpayment to deposit account number 50-1778. The Examiner is invited to telephone the below-signed attorney to discuss this application.
